title: Choosing Fonts for Your Brand: Licenses, Pairing and Custom Type
h1: Choosing fonts for your brand: licenses, pairing and custom type
description: How brand fonts work: choosing typefaces, pairing, font licenses for web, apps and print, custom lettering vs custom fonts, and what to ask a designer.
intro: Fonts shape how a brand feels long before anyone reads the words. They also come with licenses that many buyers never check, which can cause problems when a font used in a logo or website was only licensed for personal projects. Whether you are choosing fonts for a new brand, refreshing your website or considering a custom typeface, this article explains the basics, the licensing questions and when it makes sense to hire a type specialist.

faq.q: Are free fonts safe to use commercially?
faq.a: Many are, under open licenses, but some free downloads are for personal use only. Check each license.

faq.q: Does one font license cover everything?
faq.a: Usually not. Desktop, web, app, ebook and broadcast uses are often licensed separately.

faq.q: How many fonts should a brand use?
faq.a: Often two: one for headings and one for body text, sometimes with a few weights of each.

faq.q: What is the difference between lettering and a font?
faq.a: Lettering is custom drawn for one use, like a logo; a font is a full set of characters you can type.

faq.q: Who should hold the font license?
faq.a: Your business. Licenses bought by a designer may not transfer to you.
